definitions.definition: Six stations of the soul's progress to union with Śiva — bhakta (devotion has arisen), māheśvara (steadfastness through dispassion), prasādi (serenity of mind through grace), prāṇaliṅgi (the liṅga known within as consciousness whose power is breath), śaraṇa (bridal union with Śiva) and aikya (immersion in Śiva's bliss). The first three are marked by predominance of action, the last three by the yoga of knowledge.
The vacanas, above all Cennabasava's, arrange the whole of devotional life under the six sthalas, each paired with a liṅga, a kind of devotion and a mode of the soul.

relations.note: the SSM's 101 sthalas are subdivisions of the six

definitions.definition: The SSM's full map: 44 sub-sthalas on the side of the soul (bhakta 15, māheśvara 9, prasādi 7, prāṇaliṅgi 5, śaraṇa 4, aikya 4) followed by 57 on the side of the liṅga (9, 9, 9, 9, 12, 9), from piṇḍa to jñānaśūnya.

name: The six liṅgas

definitions.definition: Śiva met as six liṅgas corresponding to the six sthalas: ācāraliṅga (bhakta), guruliṅga (māheśvara), śivaliṅga (prasādi), jaṅgamaliṅga (prāṇaliṅgi), prasādaliṅga (śaraṇa), mahāliṅga (aikya); in the manual tradition each is correlated with a sense (smell, taste, sight, touch, hearing, the heart) and an element.

notes: Not set out in these terms in the SSM (whose liṅga-sthalas differ); sense and element correlations from memory of later manuals — low confidence.

definitions.definition: Devotion deepens through six forms matching the sthalas: śraddhā (faith), niṣṭhā (steadfastness), avadhāna (attentiveness), anubhava (experience), ānanda (bliss) and samarasa (equal flavour).

name: The six śaktis on the side of the liṅga

definitions.definition: In the manual scheme the liṅga's power appears as six śaktis facing the six bhaktis of the soul: kriyā, jñāna, icchā, ādi, parā and cit, from the bhakta to the aikya stage.

notes: Reconstructed from memory of ṣaṭsthala manuals; verify.

definitions.definition: The liṅga is threefold: gross (the iṣṭaliṅga worn on the body), subtle (the prāṇaliṅga of inner contemplation) and beyond the highest (the tṛptiliṅga).
The vacanas speak of iṣṭaliṅga, prāṇaliṅga and bhāvaliṅga, and the manuals correlate them with the gross, subtle and causal bodies and with the three aṅgas (tyāga, bhōga, yōga).

relations.note: correlation found in the vacana/manual tradition, not stated in SSM 6.49–50

definitions.definition: The soul in three modes across the six sthalas: tyāgāṅga (bhakta, māheśvara), bhōgāṅga (prasādi, prāṇaliṅgi), yōgāṅga (śaraṇa, aikya), facing iṣṭa-, prāṇa- and bhāva-liṅga.
The whole path is framed as the relation of the soul (aṅga, 'limb') to Śiva (liṅga): knowledge is the aṅga and the eternal knowable the liṅga; the aṅgaliṅgī has each mounted in the other.

name: Union of liṅga and aṅga (liṅgāṅga-sāmarasya, aikya)

definitions.definition: Liberation as the soul's immersion in the ocean of Śiva's bliss, free of longing for sense-pleasure; the self contemplated as dissolved in the sky of consciousness by the nature of sāmarasya; 'like water in water' in common exposition.
Death of the devotee is itself called liṅgaikya: Basava at Kūḍalasaṅgama, Allama and Akka at Kadaḷi.

name: Difference in practice, non-duality in union (SSM)

definitions.definition: The SSM assigns difference and non-difference to stages: at the māheśvara stage the worshipper rejects total non-duality because worship rests on the difference of Lord and servant, and non-duality comes only with realization (10.37–43); at aikya, difference and even lordship and boundness are seen to be imagined by māyā, and one who no longer thinks 'I am servant, Śiva master' stands in non-duality (14.8–9; 14.37). The text grounds this in its own principle that its teaching differs by sthala and by qualified aspirant (5.22–23).

name: The personal liṅga worn on the body (iṣṭaliṅga)

definitions.definition: Śiva himself, given by the guru at initiation as a small liṅga worn on the body for life and worshipped on the palm; Śiva abides in it from the moment of initiation, so it needs no invocation; the outer liṅga is to be worn 'knowing it is of that same form' as the inner.
The body bearing the liṅga is itself the temple: the moving (jaṅgama) against the fixed (sthāvara) shrine.

name: Śakti-viśiṣṭādvaita (the Vīraśaiva view of Śiva and Śakti)

definitions.definition: Śiva is one, qualified by his inseparable Śakti: the pedestal is the supreme Śakti, the liṅga Paraśiva, and the union of Śiva and Śakti — the universe — is the liṅga; the soul is qualified by devotion (bhakti) as Śiva by power (Śrīpati's formulation; philosophy owned by U16).

name: The void (śūnya, bayalu) in Allama Prabhu

definitions.definition: Allama names the ultimate as the void — bayalu, open space without enclosure — in which liṅga, aṅga and every attainment cease to be two; his tests of the other śaraṇas in the Śūnyasampādane bring each attainment to this void.

notes: Needs anchoring in specific vacanas in Phase D.

name: The fixed and the moving (sthāvara and jaṅgama)

definitions.definition: Temples, images and installed liṅgas are the fixed, which perish; the devotee's body and the wandering devotee are the moving, which endures and is the true temple; worship of stone while despising the living devotee is hypocrisy.

The SSM ranks worship on the palm above worship on a pedestal, the inner liṅga above stone liṅgas and calls those who cling only to the outer liṅga deluded, yet forbids using the nirmālya of fixed liṅgas and bids their protection.

relations.note: the iṣṭaliṅga replaces the temple liṅga

definitions.definition: Three forms of the one Śiva met by the devotee: the guru who initiates (Śiva himself present, 11.19–21), the liṅga he gives, and the jaṅgama — the moving Śivayogin whose sight, touch and worship sanctify (11.37–43); the first three of the eight shields.

name: The guru: how he is found, tested and honoured

definitions.definition: The disciple, discerning and dispassionate, seeks a guru free of greed, versed in self-inquiry and the Śiva-siddhānta, righteous, of good conduct, wearing ash, rudrākṣa and the liṅga, knowing the yoga of liṅga and aṅga (6.1–6); without a perfected guru there is no end to saṃsāra, and such gurus are rare (13.24–27); the guru is Śiva and is not to be regarded as an ordinary man (11.19–24).
Allama tests every aspirant, including Akka Mahādēvi and Siddharāma, by questioning in the assembly.

name: Liṅga-initiation

definitions.definition: The guru bathes the disciple with consecrated water, whispers the five-syllable mantra secretly into his right ear, installs a liṅga in the disciple's breath and places it in his hand, to be worn for life; dīkṣā gives knowledge and destroys the fetters and removes the duality of guru and disciple.
Initiation is open to all — women, children and every occupation; Allama received the liṅga from the yogi Animiṣa.

notes: Secrecy: the mantra is given 'secretly' (nigūḍham, SSM 6.21).

name: The Pañcācārya lineage and the transmission of the SSM

definitions.definition: Śiva taught the doctrine to the Goddess and Nandin; the gaṇa Reṇuka, emerging from the Someśvara liṅga at Kollipāki, taught Agastya; five ācāryas appear from liṅgas in every age and found the five pīṭhas; the SSM's compiler stands in the ācārya line of Muddadeva and Siddhanātha.

name: The Anubhava Maṇṭapa

definitions.definition: In the tradition's account, the hall of experience at Kalyāṇa where śaraṇas of every birth, women included, shared and tested their experience under Allama on the throne of the void.

notes: Scholarly account (labeled): known chiefly from the 15th-c. Śūnyasampādane and later hagiography; its form as a formal institution is debated.

definitions.definition: Eight protections enclosing the devotee's life: guru, liṅga, jaṅgama, pādōdaka, prasāda, vibhūti, rudrākṣa and mantra.
The SSM's bhakta-sthala includes initiation, liṅga-wearing, ash, rudrākṣa, the five-syllable mantra and the worship and prasāda of guru, liṅga and jaṅgama among its fifteen sub-sthalas.

Five codes of conduct: liṅgācāra (exclusive worship of the liṅga), sadācāra (honest livelihood and moral life), śivācāra (equality of all devotees), bhṛtyācāra (servant-humility) and gaṇācāra (defence of the community and faith).
The SSM's exclusivity (no other gods), its duty to protect liṅgas and devotees at the cost of life and its rule on revilers of Śiva are the textual background of liṅgācāra and gaṇācāra.
Honest labour in one's own occupation is worship — 'work is Kailāsa' — and must not be interrupted even for guru, liṅga or jaṅgama, nor gather beyond the day's need.

relations.note: the fruit of kāyaka is shared as dāsōha

definitions.definition: The devotee's stance 'I am your servant' rather than 'I am He', and the giving of the fruits of work to the jaṅgamas and the community; in modern maṭhas, free feeding and schooling.

name: Conduct: inner and outer purity, word and deed

definitions.definition: Do not steal, kill, lie, rage, despise others, praise yourself or blame others — inner and outer purity; compassion is the root of dharma; deeds must match words; equanimity under praise and blame.

The vacanas refuse caste among devotees: Basava calls himself the son of a cobbler's house and asks to say of every devotee 'he is ours'; the intercaste marriage at Kalyāṇa is remembered as the occasion of the upheaval.

The SSM makes devotion, not birth, the mark of the bhakta (9.4–5), tells the māheśvara to drop jāti-dharmas opposed to the liṅga (10.30–31) and sees brāhmaṇa and outcaste alike at union (14.19–20), but also prescribes eating with twice-born of one's own jāti on the path (9.29) and distinguishes Śiva's and Brahmā's orderings of varṇa and āśrama (10.34–36).
Liṅga-wearers are not subject to the pollutions of birth, death, menstruation, leftovers or caste.
The teacher who has become Śiva is not tainted by birth- and death-pollution (14.16).
Women receive the liṅga, compose vacanas and sit in the assembly; Akka Mahādēvi is examined and acknowledged by Allama; Dāsimayya teaches that the self is neither man nor woman.

Devotion is ninefold, outer and inner — setting the breath in the liṅga and the liṅga in the breath with a still mind — and arises from grace as grace arises from it; its presence, not birth, makes the bhakta; it is the power of the soul as śakti is of the liṅga (manual tradition).
Purity of mind is grace; everything to be enjoyed is first offered to the liṅga and received back as prasāda, which purifies the mind; so too the prasāda of guru and jaṅgama.

name: The devotee as bride of Śiva

definitions.definition: At the śaraṇa stage the soul is wife and Śiva husband; the śaraṇa, like a faithful wife, is turned from all else; Akka Mahādēvi lives this in her vacanas to Cennamallikārjuna.

name: The self (jīva, aṅga, ātman) in the Vīraśaiva view

definitions.definition: The jīva is a part of the formless Śiva through beginningless ignorance, with Śiva abiding in it as fire in the sunstone; the self is eternal and distinct from body, senses and intellect (against Cārvāka and Bauddha), atomic through contact with impurity, yet in truth shining like a lamp in the heart.
The mind is a mirror soiled by ignorance that the guru cleanses; serenity of mind is grace; outer impressions (vāsanā) project the world, inner ones reveal the self's bliss.
Māyā is not gold, woman or land but the desire standing before the mind.

name: Consciousness, samādhi and the void of mental activity

definitions.definition: The liṅga is consciousness (cit, saṃvit) shining within; śivayoga-samādhi is undivided attention on the supreme self as 'I am He'; in aikya the yogin abides in a heart empty of mental activity, dissolved in Śiva; the realized abides in the self through all dealings of knower, known and knowing.

notes: Waking/dream/deep sleep/fourth are not treated in the passages recorded here — gap.

name: Inner centres and the liṅga of light

definitions.definition: The liṅga of light shines at the base (mūlādhāra), in the heart and between the brows — gold, coral-red and crystal; the prāṇaliṅga rises from the navel-bulb where prāṇa and apāna meet; six centres from the base to the brows, and above them the thousand-petalled lotus with the moon-disc and the subtle aperture called Kailāsa, from which nectar cools the heart.
The manual tradition places the six liṅgas in the six centres (low confidence).

The one consciousness-brahman is imagined as enjoyer, enjoyed and impeller through the three guṇas; tamas and rajas are removed at the śaraṇa stage; earth and the other elements are Śiva's eight forms, his body and effect; the thirty-six tattvas are waves of Śiva's ocean.
Śiva is free of the three impurities; the soul is atomic through impurity and is freed when the bond of impurity is shaken off.

Born by karma into castes and burned by threefold suffering, the soul becomes pure-minded when karma ripens and Śiva's grace arises; those who bear the inner liṅga do not return; liberation while living belongs to the one who knows the liṅga as liberation; the knower's karma-seeds are burnt, his acts leave no fruit and every act is worship.
Liberation is liṅgaikya, union with the liṅga, open to all who wear it.

name: Cosmology: Śiva, Śakti and the world

definitions.definition: The thirty-six tattvas are the waves and bubbles of Śiva's ocean of consciousness; Śiva emits the pramathas; the world arises from Śiva and is not different from him; the five ācāryas appear in every yuga; the descent of Reṇuka at Kollipāki is placed in the Kali age.

name: Mantra: the five syllables and the praṇava

definitions.definition: 'Namaḥ śivāya' is the designation of Śiva and root of all mantras; the name 'Śiva' reveals brahman in its primary sense; the five syllables comprise all that exists in fives; with Oṃ it is six-syllabled; Oṃ arises from 'so'ham'; mental repetition is best.

name: The vacana as speech of experience

definitions.definition: The vacana is spontaneous speech from experience in the mother tongue, sealed with the aṅkita; speech must be pure as a string of pearls and matched by deeds.

name: Death as union with the liṅga

definitions.definition: The death of a devotee is liṅgaikya; the dead are buried seated, holding the liṅga, rather than cremated, and no ancestral rites or death-pollution follow; the saints' deaths are narrated as union at sacred places.
One who at death drinks water in which a rudrākṣa has been pressed, thinking of Rudra, goes to Rudra's world.

notes: Burial practice details are general knowledge of the community (moderate confidence), not from a cited text.

name: Powers and the warning against them

definitions.definition: Gorakṣa's indestructible body is surpassed by Allama's void body; attainment of powers is not the goal.
The five-syllable mantra is said to give all powers when uttered (8.36–43); the Śivayogin's sight gives accomplishment (11.37–43).

name: Vedic ritual and scripture in Vīraśaiva teaching

definitions.definition: Basava will put the Veda to the touchstone and fetter the śāstras; worship of the moving replaces sacrifice and temple.

The SSM upholds the Veda and Āgama as one in meaning but declares sacrifices, the Agnihotra and austerities not worth a fraction of liṅga-worship or the five-syllable mantra, and useless without devotion.
